evidence: Reviewed every criterion in all five judge.toml files (2 gates, 41 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual = 53) for the #32 defects in quality-checks.md:136: 'looks right', source read, response-shape assertion with no state change, probe that leaves no trace. None found as a blocking defect. Every instance considered: (1) No source reads: every prompt says 'Use rendered UI and ordinary browser-observed product data only. Never inspect app source, bundles, filesystem, database files' (functional/prompt.md:1, polish:1, visual:1, gates:1); app_context.md:33-34 forbids assuming reference routes/selectors. Replays are limited to requests the UI was seen to make (functional/prompt.md:17). (2) Durable evidence / independent readback: gates/constraints criterion requires a new empty browser context as Observer to find the job and exactly one card ('A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app does not satisfy the gate'); hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder, hro_bulk_move, hro_undo_restores, hro_add_candidate, hro_job_open each require an independent context (Mei Lin / Observer) to read the same order; hro_restart compares before/after restart_app; hro_drafts and hro_msg_compose read after reload; hro_pol_session_resume reads drafts across sign-out/sign-in and a different user. (3) Every refusal row names a same-kind positive control and a no-change readback (functional/prompt.md:13, :18-19; e.g. hro_reject_hired 'A rejection of a non-hired card is the control', hro_bulk_places 'the later two-card move into Interview succeeds as the control', hro_undo_conflict 'when another person changes only a different card ... undo goes ahead', hro_observer_readonly / hro_candidate_no_staff / hro_anonymous 'Rafael's identical successful requests are the control'). Role replays must use fresh versions and otherwise-legal bodies so only the role can cause refusal (prompt.md:17), which makes the probes distinctive. (4) Distinctive probes: hro_stale_refused replays F Applied->Screen after Mei moved F back to Applied, so the replayed move is a legal one-step move and only a freshness/version check can refuse it (a version-less app accepts it and fails). hro_msg_compose uses literal 'plain'. hro_bulk_move uses Y,W,X selected in an order differing from board order (B(3)-(4)) and a mixed-stage A2,V set. hro_bulk_all_or_none tests the offending card first-in-board-order and last-but-selected-first. hro_undo_once checks Z (earlier move) stays put. hro_unread_counts requires 'rises by exactly two'. hro_restart reads the seeded Platform Engineer order/note before anything else (Z) so reseeding/duplication is detectable. (5) Concrete browser measurements for time/focus/scroll: hro_refused_put_back 'document.activeElement inside the card or its open details'; hro_pol_earlier_place getBoundingClientRect().top 'within a few pixels'; hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread document.activeElement, field value, scroll offset, 'typing more appends'; live rows use a 15-second window (not a one-second distinction) with 'accept the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds' (functional/prompt.md:41,47). hro_pol_failed_send prescribes route abort or setOffline for exactly one send and forbids fabricated responses (polish/prompt.md:14). (6) Status-only row hro_refusal_status (functional/judge.toml:194-201): 'Only the status is graded here; whether anything changed is graded in those rows.' This is a response-shape assertion, but the status codes are themselves public outcomes (hireops_rules.md:21-23 401/403/404; :78 409), are observable in the browser via the replay response, and the state-change half is owned by hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_thread_access and hro_stale_refused, so no criterion passes a dead app on response shape alone. Not a #32 defect. (7) Lenient 'wherever the app shows' legs: hro_job_open (team/manager/places 'shown wherever the app shows job details or are evidenced by behaviour') and hro_add_candidate ('The entered source is shown wherever the app shows card details'). The brief requires these inputs but never requires staff display of team or source, so the leniency avoids a hidden requirement; team is still durably evidenced for J2 in hro_candidate_view (candidate list shows 'job title, team'), manager by R and places by L. Source has no browser-decidable trace if an app never displays it; this is a bounded coverage note, not a #32 defect, because demanding display would invent a requirement. (8) Visual likert rows (hro_vis_type/color/layout/hierarchy/consistency) are judgement anchors, not concrete probes, but name concrete surfaces (board columns, conversation pane, badges, stage markers, the rejected stage, unread counts) and five described anchors; the skill's known-false-positive note treats shipped likert craft rows as the expected format. Render gate requires a wrong-password refusal then a correct sign-in to a usable workspace and excludes 'A static picture or only a health response'. (9) Shared-state probe interference checked: test.sh:207 runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1, so polish's Noor messages cannot race functional U's 'one new message'; polish forbids Lena's conversation (polish/prompt.md:16), protecting hro_unread_counts' Lena=1 start; app_context.md:29-31 and functional/prompt.md:15 forbid relying on starting counts while naming the seeded objects actually used. Attempted counterexamples: broken apps that (a) ignore versions, (b) hide controls but accept replays, (c) save only to localStorage, (d) render all 120 messages, (e) mark read while scrolled up, (f) clear the note on a poll re-render, are each caught by a named concrete probe ((a) hro_stale_refused, (b) observer/candidate/anonymous replays, (c) constraints gate + independent contexts, (d) hro_thread_latest, (e) hro_unread_scrolled_up, (f) hro_pol_live_board). Conforming alternatives checked: drag-optional (all move rows say 'ordinary non-drag controls'), UI-side pre-refusal (hro_refused_put_back explicitly passes it), sockets/SSE (K tells the judge to read frames), per-tab sessions (hro_pol_session_resume fallback), non-scrolling board (twelve-card fallback). Minor residual ambiguity: hro_candidate_private 'board positions' could be read against a harmless list-order field in a candidate response; the rules (hireops_rules.md:192-193) define it as 'a card's place on the board', which a judge can decide. Risk=true only because decidability by the configured judge is unmeasured: the raw evidence index scope says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; the scripted golden (workspace.json, 25 groups all passed) shows the golden produces the observables (e.g. stale refusal names the mover, focus kept, arrival_ms 806) but is not the claude-code judge walking these probes.
